title: Wrong-person awaiting transition is not taken_over_at-guarded in SQL — a take-over landing between the token read and the UPDATE re-enters a landlord-handled row into the correction loop (r2 BLOCKER invariant, race leg)
evidence: form_handler.gleam:1235 'case row.taken_over_at != "" {' ... 1250 'sql.update_reference_call_status(config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, "", "contact_invalid", sql.ContactInitiated)' ; update_reference_call_status.sql: 'WHERE id = $1 AND status = $5::reference_call_status' (no taken_over_at guard)
detail: The wrong-person stand-down is a Gleam pre-read only: the guarded UPDATE matches on status='contact_initiated', which take-over does not change. A take-over landing between lookup and UPDATE yanks the taken-over row to awaiting_correction — the r2 blocker's exact invariant ('a bounce must NOT re-enter the correction loop on a landlord-handled row'). Every other failure writer (mark_awaiting_correction, exhaust_reference_call, find_reference_call_by_send_ref, sweep_claim_t0, sweep_advance, append_reference_call_attempt) got a SQL taken_over_at guard; this leg did not.
recommended_fix: Add 'AND taken_over_at IS NULL' to update_reference_call_status.sql's WHERE (or gate the awaiting transition in a dedicated SQL statement), matching mark_awaiting_correction.sql.
